newsitem.title: USA: Ford average 1998 prices unchanged from 1997.
newsitem.headline: Ford average 1998 prices unchanged from 1997.

text.p: Ford Motor Co. said Friday that prices on its 1998 models will be unchanged on average from 1997 models, reflecting a renewed emphasis by the auto industry to make cars more affordable.
The nation's second-largest automaker also said it was reshuffling its option packages to offer two basic versions of its most popular cars that would be fairly priced and well-equipped.

Under the new approach, Ford said its 1998 Taurus line-up will offer two sedan models, the LX and SE, and two option packages on the SE -- the comfort group and sports group. Currently, the Taurus line-up offers seven combinations, including three models and four equipment packages.
The pricing on the Taurus, based on option package, now ranges from $18,795 to $21,995, compared with $18,545 to $23,870 previously.
In addition to the Taurus, the simplified structure applies to Ford's Escort and Contour cars, as well as Mercury Tracer, Mystique and Sable car lines.
Earlier, General Motors Corp. said its average 1998 model year price will be 1.3 percent over the prior year, its smallest average price hike in more than a decade.
